BEFORE  HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE PRAMOD KUMAR AGRAWAL  ON THE 7 th OF MAY, 2025  CRIMINAL APPEAL No. 3313 of 2025  SITA RAM AND OTHERS  Versus  THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH AND OTHERS  Appearance:
 Shri Ghan Shyam Pandey - Advocate for the appellants.
Ms. Garima Tiwari - Panel Lawyer for State.
Shri Prabal Singh Rajput - Advocate for respondent No  ORDER

This is the second bail application filed by the appellants under Section 14-A(1) of SC/ST Act r/w 483 of B.N.S.S. for grant of regular bail relating to Crime No.19/2024 registered at Police Station - Mahila Thana, District Narsinghpur (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 366, 376,
376(D) and 506 of IPC and Sections 3(1)(w)(i), 3(1)(w)(ii), 3(2)(v) of SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.
Appellants are in detention since 31.08.2024.
Earlier bail application filed by the appellant No.1 was dismissed on merits and the bail application filed by appellants was dismissed as withdrawn.
2. As per the prosecution story, the allegation against the appellants is of committing rape with the prosecutrix.
On the basis of which, police has registered the case against the appellants under aforesaid offences.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:21278 2 CRA-3313-2025 3.
Learned counsel for the appellants submitted that appellants are innocent and have been falsely implicated.
They are in jail since 31.08.2024.
It submitted that FIR has been lodged after three days of the incident.
Although prosecutrix did not know the appellants earlier even then she has lodged named FIR against them.
Test Identification Parade of the appellants has been conducted after 20 days.

It is further submitted that Mahendra and other persons have committed murder of Dorilal who is the brother of appellant No.1 for which the offence under Section 302 of IPC has been registered against them and Sessions Trial No.55/2024 is pending before IV Additional Sessions Judge, District Narsinghpur.

sentences.text: Appellant No.1-Sita Ram has also sustained leg injury and therefore he was not able to go outside whereas the place where incident took place is 100 Km away from his house.
DNA report is also negative.
There is no injury on the body of the prosecutrix.
Appellants are uncle and nephew and they belongs to same family therefore it is unnatural that both the appellants have committed rape upon the prosecutrix simultaneously.
Statement of prosecutrix has been recorded before the trial Court and there is no chance of tampering with the evidence.
Charge-sheet has been filed.
The conclusion of the trial will take considerable time.
Therefore, it has been prayed that the appellants may be released on bail.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for State as well as objector have opposed the prayer for grant o f b a i l t o t h e a p p e l l a n t s a n d h a v e s u b m i t t e d t h a t N E U T R A L C I T A T I O N N O .
2025:MPHC-JBP:21278 3 CRA-3313-2025
in the statements recorded under Sections 161, 164 of Cr.P.C. and in the Court statement, the prosecutrix has stated that appellants have committed rape upon her.
This is a case of gang rape.
There is no material contradictions and omissions in the statement of prosecutrix.
Earlier bail application which was filed by the appellant No.1 was dismissed on merits by a reasoned order and there is no change in circumstances.
It is also submitted that minute appreciation of evidence cannot be done at this stage.
Hence, he prayed for rejection of bail application.
5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
6 . Looking to aforesaid facts and circumstances as well as act of appellants, I am not inclined to grant bail to the present appellants.
7. Accordingly, present CRA stands dismissed.
8. Certified copy as per rules.
